sections_target.text: Exhaust temperature differential alarm signal test

rows: Switch OFF all the switches, then connect an mV source to each of OTA, OTB separately, and connect another mV source to TX-A
Before injection, determine the mV corresponding to 400 °C, the mV corresponding to 420 °C, and the mV corresponding to 80 °C, to facilitate injection
Inject 400 °C into each of TX & OTA separately, then raise the temperature in OTA to 420 °C and observe the alarm coming in 30 seconds after reaching 420 °C, or read it directly from F12, F13
Reduce the injection in OTA to 380 °C and observe the alarm disappearing from the face of the card
If the values are not achieved, change resistor R3 (3) in the SOTJ card, then repeat the previous steps
Repeat all of this in the second channel, i.e. the injection is in TX-A and OTB and the reading is from D8, D9
Connect an mV source to each of OTA, OTB in parallel; also connect a DVM to Out, A com of either OTA, OTB, or at D6, D7; also connect the oscillator generator C1 at BO2 and measure it with the common
Inject mV until the DVM reading is 2 volts; also inject frequency until the 14HS lamp lights (4845 + 100)
Lower the mV and observe that the Failure alarm lamp lights in both SOTJ cards, and note that the DVM reading is less than 1 volt

Raise the mV again until the DVM reading is 2 volts and observe that the Failure alarm lamp does not go out, then reset it from the face of the card and observe that the Trip lamp is also lit, so reset it too from the face of the card
Disconnect the mV source from one of the channels and observe that the Failure lamp lights in the card opposite this channel.
Lower the frequency until the 14HS lamp goes out (3855 + 100) and observe that the Failure lamp goes out automatically
Reset and check that there are no alarms on the unit
Connect a 20 kΩ resistor between 41N in TX-A and the panel earth; observe the appearance of the alarm: Power supply or battery OR Exhaust thermocouple ground
Reset the alarm and check that there are no alarms on the unit

Procedures to be Carried Out
Overtemperature alarm signal test

Exhaust temperature differential alarm signal test
Switch OFF all the switches, then connect an mV source to each of OTA, OTB separately, and connect another mV source to TX-A | 1.
Before injection, determine the mV corresponding to 400 °C, the mV corresponding to 420 °C, and the mV corresponding to 80 °C, to facilitate injection | 2.
Inject 400 °C into each of TX & OTA separately, then raise the temperature in OTA to 420 °C and observe the alarm coming in 30 seconds after reaching 420 °C, or read it directly from F12, F13 | 3.
Reduce the injection in OTA to 380 °C and observe the alarm disappearing from the face of the card | 4.
If the values are not achieved, change resistor R3 (3) in the SOTJ card, then repeat the previous steps | 5.
Repeat all of this in the second channel, i.e. the injection is in TX-A and OTB and the reading is from D8, D9 | 6.
System Failure Induction
Connect an mV source to each of OTA, OTB in parallel; also connect a DVM to Out, A com of either OTA, OTB, or at D6, D7; also connect the oscillator generator C1 at BO2 and measure it with the common | 1.
Inject mV until the DVM reading is 2 volts; also inject frequency until the 14HS lamp lights (4845 + 100) | 2.
Lower the mV and observe that the Failure alarm lamp lights in both SOTJ cards, and note that the DVM reading is less than 1 volt | 3.
Raise the mV again until the DVM reading is 2 volts and observe that the Failure alarm lamp does not go out, then reset it from the face of the card and observe that the Trip lamp is also lit, so reset it too from the face of the card | 4.
Disconnect the mV source from one of the channels and observe that the Failure lamp lights in the card opposite this channel. | 5.
Lower the frequency until the 14HS lamp goes out (3855 + 100) and observe that the Failure lamp goes out automatically | 6.
Disconnect all the instruments. | 7.
Reset and check that there are no alarms on the unit | 8.
Ground Fault Detection
Connect a 20 kΩ resistor between 41N in TX-A and the panel earth; observe the appearance of the alarm: Power supply or battery OR Exhaust thermocouple ground | 1.
Disconnect the resistor | 2.
Reset the alarm and check that there are no alarms on the unit | 3.

uncertain_terms.note: Source spells the meter 'Fluk 187' (presumably Fluke 187); kept verbatim as in the source.
Source 'يرفض' (literally 'refuses') is garbled OCR for 'OFF'; rendered as 'switch OFF all the switches'.
Source procedure cell reads 'aالمعايرة السنوية' (stray leading 'a'); rendered as 'Annual calibration'.
Source table cell 'ر1 (1)' is garbled OCR for 'R1 (1)'; rendered as 'R1 (1)'.
Source 'تكس-أ و أوتب' is garbled OCR for 'TX-A and OTB'; rendered as such.
Source 'x400 C' / 'x420 C' rendered as '400 °C' / '420 °C' (the 'x' is OCR noise for the degree sign).
Source writes frequency tolerances with '+' (e.g. '4845 + 100'); kept verbatim — evidently '±'.
The source credits the review to 'المهندسة/ عبد المنعم الأمام' (feminine title with a masculine name); rendered as 'Eng. Abdel Monem El-Emam'.
